flagged.evidence: [[def-dirichlet-l-function]] defines the Dirichlet series only for "Re s>1". Step 1.1 nevertheless says that substitution "into the defining Dirichlet series at s=1 yields L(1,chi_4)". Its dependencies contain no result proving convergence at the boundary or identifying that conditional series with the continued L-function; the available nonprincipal-continuation theorem is not cited.

Step 2.1 asserts that, after choosing ell in the same local square classes as M, "t:=r/ell has the same local square classes on S, while outside S every odd valuation becomes even except possibly at ell." This reverses the required parity correction. With S empty, r=6, M=6, and ell=5 (the stated local condition is vacuous), t=6/5 has odd valuations at 2, 3, and 5, not only possibly at ell.

Step 2.1 replaces the load-bearing argument by "The classical ternary descent now applies" and asserts a new locally equivalent diagonal form with strictly smaller |ab|+|ac|+|bc|. Neither the descended form, its local preservation, nor the strict reduction is constructed or follows from [L2] or [L4], which only supply one-place isotropy and weak approximation.

The induction step says "The same matching argument" supplies a common global represented square class and that larger subforms are automatically locally isotropic away from finitely many places. No matching argument was established in step 1.1, and [L2] and [L3] do not prove the asserted local representation or induction reduction. Thus the global induction is not licensed.

Step 2.1 lists only the cases "(-1,p)", "(-1,-1)", "(2,p)", and "(p,q) for distinct odd primes" before concluding "every generator pair" is covered. For the stated generators -1, 2, and the odd primes, it omits (-1,2), (2,2), and (p,p). No identity reducing those diagonal or exceptional pairs to the listed cases is supplied, though they can be checked directly from the local formulas.

The theorem permits degenerate nonzero forms, but step 1.1 says to "Exclude the finite set of primes dividing 2a_1\cdots a_n." For the allowed form q=X_1^2 on a three-dimensional space, diagonalization has a_2=a_3=0, so every prime divides that product and the claimed set is not finite. The proof needs a separate zero-coefficient/isotropic case.

Step 1.1 says that "The same logarithmic character-average ... differentiates to show A(x)=phi(q)^{-1} log x+O_q(1)." Its cited [L1] supplies only the unweighted boundary asymptotic for sum p^{-s}; differentiating an O(1) asymptotic is not justified and does not yield the weighted partial-prime sum. The subsequent Abel-summation calculation depends on this unproved estimate.

For the alpha=beta=1 case, step 2.1 obtains the value by "multiplying the previous two cases and the sign coming from (p,p)_p=(-1/p)". The listed inputs establish only square-class reduction and square criteria; they neither establish bilinearity nor prove the special value (p,p)_p=(-1/p). Bilinearity is only asserted later as a consequence of this formula.

After reducing to representatives, step 2.1 says only "one checks directly" that the formula holds and delegates the claimed finite verification to Sutherland's lecture notes. [L1] and [L2] provide the reduction but no evaluations of the Hilbert symbol on the representative pairs, so the displayed formula is not proved on the current disk.
